newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs capped by 137.80 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs capped by 137.80 resistance.

text.p: September BTP futures on LIFFE recorded minor gains at the open on Tuesday but resistance at 137.80 is likely to block upside prospects, analysts said.
"Quite how far it can extend is dubious as daily momentum indicators are diverging bearishly on a near term basis," said Louise Jones, fixed income analyst at Technical Data.

The contract set a double intraday high at 137.80 on Tuesday and the more it struggles there the more it is likely to extend the corrective tone downwards, Jones said. But she added that losses would also be limited to around 137.00 for Tuesday.
By 0740 GMT, September BTP was 0.04 down at 137.45.
Analysts said despite BTPs' rangebound pattern, current low trading volumes meant price action after the U.S. employment cost index due later on Tuesday could be exaggerated.

Jones pegged minor support at 137.30, a trading level on July 22, but unless the September contract pierced 137.00, which is around the top of the previous trading range, losses should be well contained for Tuesday, she said.
Below 137.00, support could intervene at 136.70 from a trend line drawn from the beginning of the month.
Meanwhile if 137.80 went, the July 25 high of 138.10 could be secured, she said.
"Above here I can see that being a struggle," said Jones.
Nico Bakker, technical analyst at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett in Amsterdam, said the slide since the contract high of July 23 of 138.44 was a corrective phase within the uptrend move.
He saw first support at 137.18, based on the upward sloping trend line and the previous stops. If this failed, the next major support was around 135.40, the bottom in mid-July.
"If 137.18 holds we'll move up again and re-test 138.44," Bakker said, adding that the uptrend could extend to 140.00 and even higher in the short term.
By 0805 GMT, September Eurolira was 0.02 down at 93.25.
